record_notes.DCP-LETT-1870F: May 9, supplied 1856 corroborated by endorsement; all three blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Complete four-page request despite F suffix. Asks frequency, repeated sightings, beginning of record, seasonal migration timing and possible arrival of already resident species. Assumption each species arrived only once explicitly conditional for a crude average, not empirical rate. Supposes no regular migrants and seeks confirmation. Prior published list read, not this new answer already received.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1883: May 31, 1856 damaged twelve-page ALS; all eighty blocks, all twelve notes including complete modern taxonomic gloss, every annotation and bibliography independently read. Four specified winter stays limit personal observation to October–May; Lowe and other qualified reports are separate. Marked offprint uses pen mark for personally seen birds and o for reliable indirect records; full marked offprint not reproduced. P3–73 individually read: frequencies vary from tentative annual/multiyear occurrences to single sightings, unknown counts, captivity escape possibility and unverified breeding. Wind explanation is probabilistic, seabirds excepted; exhausted swallows/turtle dove ship encounter personally described. Absence from comparative lists is not proven geographic absence. P75 explicitly lacks data about new arrivals of resident species; possible/probable differs from evidence. P76 names resident breeders always found there, not observed seasonal migrants. P80 supplies Hastings dateline. Raw historical spellings, modern synonym gloss and Darwin undated crosses/coloured scoring kept separate. Source apparatus supposes prior question missing but 1870F now preserves it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1885F: June 1, supplied 1856 with endorsement; both blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Complete three-page thanks for detailed answer and received separate paper, already known in journal/book. Scientific applications are direct island colonisation and possible seed transport by feet/beak/crops, not newly proven dispersal mechanisms. Unique immediate answer to 1883, not merely generic thanks. Origin citation and prior June 1855 reading notebook are editorial layers.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1900F: June 12, supplied 1856 with endorsement; all five blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Five-page damaged letter, genuine gaps retained, not truncated solely because F suffix. Responds to missing Harcourt permission note after June 1. Wollaston published island-size claim and Gould via Wollaston shorter migrant-wing statement are reported attributions, not Harcourt observations. Asks comparison of Madeira birds/swallow wings and access to rock-pigeon/darker skins if Mason fails. Mason letter missing. Later editorial identification of darker C. trocaz not silent replacement of Darwin variety wording.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1909F: June 24, supplied 1856 with endorsement; five blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing Harcourt offer; planned London/Leadbeater and possible museum comparison not yet completed, permission to borrow requested. Egypt travel conditional; ancient-dog continuity claim from Nott/Gliddon expressly doubted, seeks investigation. Persian skins on their way versus hoped India/China breeds and requested adult Egyptian pigeons distinct. Repayment and skinning offers are prospective. August London visit in apparatus does not backdate completed June comparison.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1451: August 19, supplied 1856, recipient/year established by content and reading notebook; all seven blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Asks conditional loan of Brehm to inspect species splitting; prior skim ten years earlier not fresh full reading. P5 now reports actual museum comparison: goldfinch/linnet/greenfinch smaller, not blackbird or swift; do not generalise all birds. Wishes he had compared more. P4 recalls Harcourt facts but current book-loan request is not directly answered by surviving incoming. Numerical ID does not determine date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-4598: August 23, supplied 1856; both blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Actual Brehm physical receipt acknowledged, return in two or three weeks planned, not completed. Both 1451 and this record are Darwin outgoing, missing dispatch/cover cannot be synthesized. Reading notebook August 30 a different event from August 23 custody; unusual numeric ID must not drive chronological sorting.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2182F: December 13, supplied 1857 with endorsement; all five blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing pigeon-breeding offer; prospective show visit, four precise plumage questions, requested cross-fertility test if breed distinct, not reported completed trial. Theory all breeds from rock pigeon framed as Darwin argument. P2 explicitly rethanks earlier Madeira answer, later acknowledgment rather than new unique current incoming. Dead-bird skin offer conditional. P4–5 are attached printed shipping form with handwritten corrections per apparatus, historical instructions not research commands. Later 1858 show, 1881 breed account and 1891 recollection remain later provenance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2184F: December 15, supplied 1857 with endorsement; all three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Declines missing invitation and loan offer due health/travel burden; future Crystal Palace viewing and spring offspring conditional. Suspects unimproved Barbs, not established identity; later classification distinguishes Barbs and African owls. Persia/India carrier and tumbler skins now possessed, unlike hoped June arrivals, but no exact arrival date follows. Same-Darwin December 13 inquiry is not incoming answer.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
